content.comment_body: I've encountered an issue with [product_name] ([version_no], FW [version_no]) where the web server doesn't properly update the [product_name] display: the cursor keys are missing from the screen, making it impossible to browse messages. Testing with Chrome, Opera, and IE yielded similar results. This seems related to earlier problems described in [document]. The only way to restore proper function was to power cycle the device. Has anyone experienced similar?
Is [product_name] AccessTool or another web browser connected to [product_name]? The connection is limited.

No, AccessTool was not used and no other browsers were connected. The web server wasn't completely unusable: System, Variable, and BM screens updated as expected, but on the [product_name] display (TD/TDE) screen, the display and cursor buttons were not refreshed. The system had been running for around 50 days when I noticed, but I can't determine exactly when the issue started.

This could be due to the browser's memory. Try installing a browser you haven't used before (such as Chrome or Firefox). Delete all cookies, history, and related data. If everything is cleared, it should work correctly. Hope this helps.
The topic starter wrote: All three browsers had the same issue with cookies, history, and other data?

I typically use Chrome to access [product_name]. To verify, I also tested with Opera and IE. Since I restarted the device, I can't test clearing cache and cookies until the problem happens again. The device is in a remote location, so a method to restart it over the network would be quite helpful. I've started a support request as suggested.

Update: I received a response from [company_name] Technical Support. They stated the issue isn't known to them, and based on customer feedback, the web server should work correctly. They're suspecting a browser-related problem and requested more details such as screenshots and a description of how to reproduce it. If this is a recurring issue like with previous hardware versions, we'll need to wait for it to happen again.

Update 2: The issue reappeared in another device with FW [version_no] ([version_no]). I obtained screenshots with the browser console showing some error messages and sent them to [company_name] for analysis, awaiting their reply. Checked the German forum and noticed someone else encountered a similar issue: system crashes after around 50 days.

Hi, the procedure is always similar. When connecting to [product_name] web server via browser, the browser might retain something in memory, affecting the display of the page. Try uninstalling and reinstalling the browser, then connect to the web server before anything else. This should load all content fresh and display everything correctly.

I installed Opera anew but it didn't solve the problem. It's impractical to reinstall the browser each time. I haven't come across any other webpage needing this. HTTP is a stateless protocol, so forcing a reload with Ctrl+F5 should prompt the browser to reload all data from the server.
I've already initiated a support request. [company_name] says they can't reproduce the issue and no other customers have reported it.

I have 64 units of [product_name] with [product_name] displays, running various firmware remotely. Never noticed the issue you described. However, I have encountered the bug where after about 50 days the display stops responding, resolved by power cycling every first of the month using a spare relay output (only affected older versions).
Hi, as mentioned, your device kept running for 50 days. Does a power cycle resolve the issue?

Yes, as noted before, power cycling restores normal function. This workaround doesn't actually solve the root problem. Since these devices are installed remotely at customer sites, manually cycling power isn't practical. As far as I know, [product_name] cannot be restarted remotely using [product_name] SoftComfort or similar tools. Installing an external timer switch to automate power cycling is an option, but the manufacturer should address this bug.

I've experienced a similar issue, occurring only on [product_name] [version_no]. Earlier versions, like [version_no], are unaffected. Power cycling solves the issue for approximately 50 days. [company_name]'s response to a service request was that it's not a known problem, and no action has been taken so far. I replaced a [product_name] [version_no] with a new [product_name] [version_no]; I'll see in a few weeks if the problem is resolved. Regards, [user_name]
Hi [user_name], if this issue occurs again, try using your smartphone or a different PC to connect to the web server. This could clarify if the problem originates on your PC. Hope that helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report a recurring issue where the [product_name] web server fails to update UI elements like cursor keys on the [product_name] display after extended uptime (about 50 days), preventing navigation through messages. Other screens continue working properly, but power cycling is the only temporary fix. The problem happens across different browsers and clearing browser data doesn't resolve it, pointing away from cache issues. This behavior resembles earlier device revision problems. [company_name] support is not aware of the issue and seeks more diagnostic data, suggesting this may be an intermittent firmware or runtime problem.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect stable and reliable remote monitoring and control of [product_name] devices via the web interface without physical intervention. They seek a method to restart devices remotely and rely on UI elements—like those on the [product_name] display—always rendering and updating as intended.
